summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived excerpt on the University of Chicago covering three areas: notable literary alumni, the university's early affiliation program with smaller regional colleges, and its off-campus facilities. It notes that in the early 1950s declining applications due to crime and poverty in Hyde Park led the university to sponsor an urban renewal project, and that an early entrant program was adopted alongside Shimer College. The affiliation program of the 1890s, including its terms and eventual end by 1910, is described in detail. The note closes by listing the university's overseas and Chicago-area centers, including Singapore, London, Paris, Beijing, New Delhi and Hong Kong.
one_line: Overview of the University of Chicago's literary alumni, 1890s college affiliation program, early urban renewal role, and international campuses.
key_facts: Notable literary alumni named in the note include Lauren Oliver, Philip Roth, Saul Bellow, Allan Bloom, Studs Terkel, Susan Sontag, Richard Rorty and Kurt Vonnegut.
Saul Bellow is described as a Canadian-born Pulitzer Prize and Nobel Prize for Literature winning writer.
Allan Bloom is described as the author of the New York Times bestseller "The Closing of the American Mind".
In the early 1950s, student applications declined because of increasing crime and poverty in the Hyde Park neighborhood.

In response to declining applications, the University of Chicago became a major sponsor of a controversial urban renewal project for Hyde Park that profoundly affected the neighborhood's architecture and street plan.
The university adopted an early entrant program during the early 1950s, alongside Shimer College and 10 others, allowing very young students to attend college.
In the 1890s, the University of Chicago affiliated with Des Moines College, Kalamazoo College, Butler University, and Stetson University, fearing its resources would injure smaller schools.
In 1896, the University of Chicago affiliated with Shimer College in Mount Carroll, Illinois.
Under the affiliation terms, the University of Chicago agreed to confer a degree on any graduating senior from an affiliated school who made a grade of A for all four years.
Affiliated schools were required to make no faculty appointment without the University of Chicago's approval.
Several University of Chicago professors disliked the affiliation program because it involved uncompensated additional labor and they believed it cheapened the university's academic reputation.
The affiliation program passed into history by 1910.
The Booth School of Business maintains campuses in Singapore, London, and the downtown Streeterville neighborhood of Chicago.
The Center in Paris is located on the left bank of the Seine in Paris and hosts undergraduate and graduate study programs.
In fall 2010, the University of Chicago opened a center in Beijing, near Renmin University's campus in Haidian District.
A center in New Delhi, India opened in 2014, and a center in Hong Kong opened in 2015.
